title: Fern's Prime Number Puzzle
markdown:
Every grand adventure begins with a little puzzle, and this one started with Fern the hedgehog in a terrible tizzy. Her Super-Sparkle Dewdrop Soup competition was tomorrow, and the most vital ingredient, the shimmering Moonpetal Mist, was locked away.

Fern nudged a contraption of shiny brass with her snout. Mysterious dials spun. The lock would not budge. Callum, whose mind sometimes felt like a tangled ball of yarn when numbers were involved, fiddled with four circular dials, each marked from one to ten. “It’s no ordinary lock,” Fern squeaked, spines rustling like dry leaves.

A warm voice chimed like a well-loved instrument. “Ah, but here’s the thing about that lock.” Dr Ada Brook bustled over, apron dusted with whimsical glitter. “It’s a prime number lock.” Her eyes twinkled. “Prime numbers are particular. They don’t split evenly into smaller matching groups.”

She held up a smooth stone. “This is a prime stone. You can’t break it evenly into smaller identical pieces. Only itself, and one.” Then another stone with faint lines. “This is composite. It breaks easily. Four is two and two. Nine is three and three.”

She drew on the dusty floor. “The lock only accepts numbers like my prime stones. Numbers that can only be divided by themselves and by one. One doesn’t count as prime. It is the lonely starter, not the rebel.”

Callum looked at the dials. One through ten. He pictured the unbroken prime stone. Two. Three. Five. Seven. Four? Two groups of two. Six? Three groups of two. Eight, two groups of four, or four twos. Nine, three threes. Ten, two fives. His stomach did a little flip-flop, then settled. A warm certainty. “The numbers that work are two, three, five, and seven.”

Fern nudged him. “The code, Callum. Quickly.”

He took a steadying breath. The dials already showed a two, a three, a five, and a seven, waiting as if they had been patient all along. “These are all prime. The lock needs a sequence of prime digits. So the code is two, three, five, seven.”

Clicks. A gentle whirr. The contraption sprang open. Inside, on velvet, lay the shimmering Moonpetal Mist. Fern let out a joyous squeak.

Ada smiled, no sermon, only the glitter on her apron catching the light. “You found the primes. They don’t break into smaller matching teams. That’s all the lock wanted.”

Callum beamed, a new steadiness blooming, bright as the mist. He had sorted the numbers, opened the box, and saved the soup. Fern was already planning the garnish. Tomorrow’s competition, at least, would not fail for want of Moonpetal — and Callum wondered, looking at the unused ones and eights, what other locks might be waiting for numbers that refused to split.
characters: Callum (a calm experimenter), Fern (a hedgehog), Ada (a doctor)
author: StoryGen Community
